summary: The grades were not quite comparable: the written rules (four times the rules in every session, half of them hidden from search, no budget) and the build (five type checks a push, nothing held, one deploy already killed for memory) carry the same kind of waste as the owner's browser and become a D, so five D and eight C stand. The thirteen cards gave different numbers for the same thing in about twenty places; each now has one, mostly the stricter (the AI round, a product view, the page list, admin words on a store page, the motion styles), and a bar was loosened where it asked for more than an A needs (the admin kit's counts, a hold on tests' copies, the 8-minute job, a first push's cold type check, 1,700 modules for a product page, words counted as read at load). Of the 73 shortfalls, 53 tighten a step the plan already has, 15 become new steps (four of them before opening: a hold on CLAUDE.md, four scheduler jobs at a time, the 800 px copy for pictures in pages, and themes that write today's page shape), 4 are merged into another area's and 1 is answered by moving the bar; none is dropped. In the plan itself, step 0.36 must not delete the server side of a feature that only lacks a screen, step 0.19 hides a question about 'select all', a listing's per-product database calls move from the last phase to phase 2, and every script a check rests on must leave the scratch folder for the repo. No step is missing for an A in every area, but six of your answers must be a yes (the feature index out of CLAUDE.md, a store's domain looked up on request, a bound on what a listing fetches ahead, one kaizenaflow.com, the AI manager's 17 extra tools on demand, the notice badge up to ten minutes late), the build may need a larger machine, and nobody has yet shown a themed store page at 90 on a slow phone.
